events.name: Noon
events.intro: Studio one. A glass booth. A clock with a red second hand: eleven fifty-eight. A desk; a microphone on a spring arm; a script, one page, typed, corrected, corrected back. The last line: "Giovanni. Team Rocket calls you home." Through the glass: Archer, with his hands behind his back. Ariana at the door. Petrel, with no wig on, which nobody's seen before. Proton, looking at the floor. Behind them, the whole of the Return that would fit in a corridor: Mika at the front, with a folded paper; Mr. Sallow, with his cap in his hand; Tobi. On the roof, over all their heads: a man in an iron mask, and a black ball, and air that's the wrong season. The second hand. Archer, through the talkback, very gently: "When the light's red. Just as it's written. Or— as you find you can." The light's red. Every radio in Johto is on. The Final Choice is what you say into it.

success.text: You read it as written, on every band in Johto. The Tower hums. In the corridor a hundred and fifty people are holding their breath, and one of them is fourteen.

choices.label: "This is the Radio Tower. Here's where the Director is. Here's where the mast is. Here's the hideout."

branches.text: You, on every band: "The real Director's in the basement store room. The mast's on a barge at the Lake of Rage. The hideout's under the souvenir shop in Mahogany; push the Gyarados's eye." Through the glass, nobody moves. For a whole second, nobody at all. Then Ariana shuts the studio door, from the outside, and stands in front of it. Ariana: "Nobody goes in till they've finished. I said I'd back whoever held the microphone."

Through the glass: a hundred and fifty faces. Mika's dropped her paper. Archer has his eyes shut, and his shoulders have come down, for the first time in three years. Archer, on the talkback, off the air, barely a voice: "...Thank you. I couldn't have said it."

remembers.notice: Mika, at the front of the corridor, isn't looking at the clock. She's looking at Archer.
Somebody has chalked the fourth rule on the corridor wall, under the three: "Give it back when they can pay."

events.intro: Goldenrod's police and the Tower's guards come up the stairs, and Gym trainers who "heard the broadcast and came to end it." You post the squad. Mika is at your elbow, waiting to be told where.

success.text: In the lobby, Old Rocket don't fight. They stand in a row with their caps off and sing the closing-time song, and the police stop: nobody's ever been sung at. Tobi has wired the Broadcast Keys so each needs one turn, not two. Mika is behind the glass, safe, and she sees everything. The stairs are yours.

success.text: The lobby and the studio come up the stairs to meet you.

events.name: Phase 2: The Broadcast Keys
events.intro: Three keys. The Tower hums louder with each one seated.

success.text: Archer, on the PA: "One. He could hear me through a tin can." The hum climbs. Archer: "Two. Boss, if the line's bad, I'll say it again." It climbs. Archer: "Three. Then I'll stop asking."

events.name: Phase 3: The Rival
events.intro: Your rival bursts out of the stairwell. "You read it. I heard you read it. I was in a tea shop. Everyone stopped stirring."

success.text: "Then it can be one day without you in it."

choices.label: "Go and get Mary out. Third floor."

success.text: No battle. Your rival looks at you for one long second, and goes. It's this ending's one mercy.
The two of you stand by the big speaker. The carrier hiss. A minute. "...There's nothing." "Not yet." Your rival doesn't fight. They stay.

events.name: Phase 4: The Defender
events.intro: Goldenrod's Gym Leader leads the last of them up the stair. Whitney: "Pull the plug, Rocket. People are listening."

success.text: At half her ace's health the Tower goes to Dead Air, and she doesn't flinch.

events.name: Phase 5: The Roof
events.intro: Noon's been and gone. Nothing's come back on any band. The dish; the man in the iron mask on the rail; the black ball. Archer, on the stair, hoarse: "Nothing. Not even static." He looks up. Archer: "It doesn't matter. I made other arrangements. Standby: if I go through, hold the roof for ten minutes. If I don't come back—" He doesn't finish. The man in the iron mask: "And here's my favourite part of every job. The part where I explain that it's mine now." Celebi is in the Ball, in three Thorn Rings. You aren't freeing it. You're deciding whether Archer gets his door.

success.text: You fight the man in the iron mask for the Ball.

success.text: You fight the man in the iron mask for the Ball, and win it, and hold it out. Archer looks at the door for a long moment. Archer: "I've had my answer. Four lines, three years late. I don't need to stand in a doorway to hear it again." He doesn't go through.

success.text: The three rings, one by one, and the Ball splits. Celebi is free. Archer watches his door close. He sits down on the cable drum. Archer: "...Thank you. I think. I'd have stood in that doorway for ever. I can see that now. It's not a kindness I'd have done myself."

Archer turns. The Heir is on the stair, in white trim, furious about it. The Heir: "It's a nice coat. That's the worst part. Don't make it mean anything." Archer puts the Dark Ball down on the rail himself. Archer: "I don't need the door. I've somebody to make the room ready for." The man in the iron mask takes his fee and goes, laughing.

events.name: Phase 5: The Door
events.intro: The Ball is Archer's. The roof is three years ago for as long as it takes him to step, and he's gone. You hold the roof alone, ten turns, against the police. At the tenth he's back, standing exactly where he was. His coat's wet. Archer: "I stood in the door. The lobby. That night. There was a child on the steps."

success.text: Archer: "I couldn't. They were so certain. They'd a Pokémon that kept looking up at them to see if they were all right. I thought: if I stop this one, I've to be the kind of man who stops that. And he wasn't worth it. I stood in the door of the building, and I worked out, three years late, that he wasn't worth it." Archer: "So I stepped aside. I've just watched you go up the stairs. It's the best thing I've ever done, and nobody was there."

He looks at you properly. Archer: "It was you. Smaller." Then the rest of it, the certain child and the Pokémon looking up, and the man in the door who stepped aside. Archer: "It's the best thing I've ever done, and nobody was there."

The Yateses sell candy bars, and are asked their opinion, weekly. Archer would be your Patron, if asked: "Tell me whose room." Ariana was asked, and stopped the tails that day. Petrel is nobody, and finding out who that is. Proton is the one who says "stop." The Heir sits on the arm of the chair. The Marauder goes unpaid: the ring's redeemed instead. Kurt has the Ball, to open in his own time. Giovanni hears there's a new chair, and says nothing; which, from him, is approval.

events.name: The Verdict
events.intro: Your lead is down. Archer switches the microphone off. Archer: "Not today. Executive, then."

choices.label: Take the coat he gives you.

success.text: He holds out a white-trimmed coat, not his. Archer: "You held. I knew you would. The Boss will hear of this." A pause; it's the old line, and he hears himself. Archer: "...I've heard of it. That'll have to do. Executive. Welcome to what's left of the family." Johto is listening. The Return holds the airwaves, and what they carry is up to Archer, a man who's just found out he was wrong. It plays music. It reads the weather, correctly. Once a day, at noon, a voice says: "Team Rocket. Standing by." Nobody knows what for any more; it's become a time signal. You wear a white-trimmed coat. Mika believes he heard. Tobi tends the mast, badly, for ever. Mr. Sallow goes home; he's taken the hint. Sabela dusts the chair. The Director reads what he's given. Mary is on air, under guard. The Yateses sell candy bars to Rocket. Archer is wrong, and knows it, and reads the weather. Ariana is passed over again. Petrel is the Director, for good; it's the saddest one. Proton does the tails. The Heir hears his father was called, and wasn't there. The Marauder is paid in full. Kurt never speaks to you again. Somewhere, a phone rings once, and nobody speaks.

events.name: Team Static
events.intro: A houseboat on the canal at Goldenrod, with a washing line that's actually an aerial. A man of seventy in a cardigan, and a camp stove. The Director: "I let myself out. Forty years in that building; I know which door they haven't found. They've a fellow in my office wearing my face. He's got my walk wrong. I shuffle. He strides." The Director: "I've forty years of knowing how to run a station, and a tower I can't go back to. You've a way of turning up where things are happening. Let's be a nuisance."

success.text: The Director: "The true sort. Out loud, where everyone can hear." He paints it on the hull that week: "Say what's true, out loud, where everyone can hear." The call sign is a kettle whistling. Within the week there's a crew: the Director (voice: "I won't broadcast a thing I haven't checked twice."), Buena from the password show (heart: "There's always cake."), Tobi Northcott, demoted for mercy, who walked (hands: "I won't make it look broken. I'll break it."), and the Yateses from the souvenir shop (eyes: "We don't ask."). They've been listening through the floor for three years. They know everything.

He lifts a tarpaulin. A transmitter the size of a suitcase, older than you. The Director: "My first. 1961. It reaches about as far as you can shout. We'll need to shout from a great many places." Within the week there's a crew, and a kettle for a call sign.
The Director: "Nobody, yet. That's the beauty of it. Everyone who listens will have chosen to." The Yateses come aboard with a tray. Tobi comes with a soldering iron. Buena brings cake.

events.name: Broadcast 1: This Is Mary
events.intro: The Black Hour. Midnight. Mary's reading Rocket's coded orders under guard. Static is going to jam it, from a van in the Tower's own car park, and put her through on the pirate band instead. The Director, in the van, with headphones: "She's saying "the kettle's on at the usual place." That's Olivine. I've had the code since week two; it's the shipping forecast with the sea areas swapped. Amateurs."

choices.label: Get the suitcase to the roof of the car park.

success.text: It's heavier than it looks.

events.name: The Car Park Roof
events.intro: The top level of the car park, in the rain, with a suitcase and a hundred feet of cable. Tobi is turning a dial very slowly.

choices.label: Hold it while Tobi finds the frequency.

success.text: A Signal Technician has found you first, with a Noctowl.

events.name: The Switch
events.intro: Tobi has it. Tobi: "There. Your hand. You do it."

success.text: Every radio in Johto: a whistle, like a kettle. Mary, who can hear it in her headphones, and knows what it is: "...This is Mary. Not the one you've been hearing. The real one. I'm on the third floor of the Radio Tower. The weather's been wrong for a month, and I'm sorry. Here's what the forecasts meant." She reads the code, decoded, for four minutes. Then the guard's hand is on her shoulder, and she's still talking. By morning there's a queue at the Tower's front desk, of people who'd like to speak to Mary, please, and aren't leaving. She walks out through them, and comes to the houseboat. Mary: "I won't read a script I didn't write. Never again."

remembers.notice: Afterwards you tell Mary: "There's a girl of seven who's written you nine letters." Mary: "...That's who they're from. They're pinned over my desk. They were the only post that wasn't orders."

events.name: Broadcast 2: The Price of a Tail
events.intro: The Slowpoke Well itself. Kurt, with a bad back, carrying the aerial. Kurt: "I've shouted at them for a month. I've a voice that carries to my own front gate. Give me that thing."

success.text: Kurt, on air, to the whole of Johto: "A million. That's what they're charging. D'you know what it costs the Slowpoke? Ask it. Here." He holds the microphone to Old Yawn. It yawns. It's the longest, saddest, most reasonable sound anyone's heard on a wireless. Buena, afterwards: "Password for today is "TAIL." Say it back. It's worth a prize. The prize is: don't buy one." It rains on Azalea. No shop in Johto will stock them now.

events.name: Broadcast 3: Not Known at This Address
events.intro: The hardest one. It's addressed to Archer. The Yateses, who have been listening through the floor: "He pawned his mother's ring in the spring. He doesn't know we know. He brings the tea tray back every single night. We'd like to say something to him. We don't know how." You write it: three lines, from five.

choices.label: "Mr. Archer. This is the shop upstairs." / "We know about the watch, and the flat, and the ring."

success.text: Two lines down.

choices.label: "Mr. Archer. This is the shop upstairs." / "He isn't coming. You've known a year. So have we."

success.text: Two lines down.

choices.label: "We know about the watch, and the flat, and the ring." / "He isn't coming. You've known a year. So have we."

success.text: Two lines down.

events.name: Not Known at This Address
events.intro: And the last line.

choices.label: "You fed a hundred and fifty people every Friday for three years. You did. Not him."

success.text: It goes out at midnight, on the pirate band, to one listener. In the chair room, a radio's on. Nobody ever finds out what he did when he heard it. In the morning the tea tray's come back, as always. There's a note on it: "Thank you. Noon. I have to see it through. — A."

choices.label: "The chair's only a chair. Come up and have a candy bar."

success.text: It goes out at midnight, on the pirate band, to one listener. In the chair room, a radio's on. Nobody ever finds out what he did when he heard it. In the morning the tea tray's come back, as always. There's a note on it: "Thank you. Noon. I have to see it through. — A."

events.name: Two Frequencies
events.intro: Noon. The Tower broadcasts the Call. The houseboat broadcasts everything else. On the same frequency. Archer's voice, from the Tower: "Giovanni. Team Rocket calls you home." Mary's, from a canal: "This is Radio Static. Here's the news. It's true; we checked it twice." The map of Johto, with two rings spreading over it. Town by town, each radio picks one. A town with a kindness in it tunes to the kettle. A town you walked through tunes to the Tower.

branches.text: Most of Johto is on Static. In the Tower, the Grunts have the pirate band on, in the corridor, turned up. Archer is speaking to an empty frequency. He stops, mid-sentence. He listens. He hears Mr. Sallow, on the houseboat, singing the closing-time song, with the words explained.
It's even. The two signals cross; for a minute every radio in Johto is playing both. Then Old Yawn yawns into the microphone, and it rains, and Static's the one that carries.

success.text: The Call goes out whole. Nothing answers. Static reads that out too: "Twelve-oh-four. No reply." It's the truth. That's the job.

events.name: The Roof
events.intro: Not a raid. The Director, Mary, Kurt, Tobi, the Yateses with a tray. And the man in the iron mask. The man in the iron mask: "What's this? A tea party?" Mrs. Yates: "Would you like a candy bar, dear? You look as though nobody's offered you anything in years that you hadn't to take." He doesn't know what to do with it.

success.text: At the third ring, Kurt says the name.

battle.name: The man in the iron mask

events.name: Off the Air
events.intro: Celebi is free. The roof is quiet, apart from a kettle somebody has brought up on the camp stove.

branches.text: Archer is on the stair. Archer: "I heard you. Last night. On the little band. I'd have had the door, and I'd have stood in it for ever, and you sent me a tea tray." He's laughing. It's not a sound he's used. Archer: "Come down. All of you. I'll put the kettle on. I've only ever been any good at making a room ready." The Return isn't beaten. It's gone off the air. The Tower is Mary's. The pirate band stays up, because the Director doesn't trust a station with only one voice on it. Mika reads the children's hour, and checks it twice. Tobi is the engineer. Mr. Sallow sings the closing-time song on air, and explains it. Sabela keeps the houseboat spotless. The Director is station manager, at seventy. Mary is the Voice. The Yateses have a wireless on the counter; it's always on. Archer works the souvenir shop's till, and he's very good with it; the coat hangs on the back of the door. Ariana sends Static the Return's books, anonymously; everyone knows. Petrel does voices on the children's hour, and all of them are his own. Proton is the first caller to the phone-in, doesn't give his name, and says sorry. The Heir listens every night and never writes in. The Marauder is offered a candy bar. Kurt: "Give me that thing." Giovanni hears a kettle on the wireless, and listens to the end.
